# Packaged quantum tuples and explicit unitors

This integration implements the next contract recorded in Issue #43, within
edition 2026. The selected hierarchy admits exact recursive Unit/Bit/Bits/tuple
bases and Op<tuple> providers. Binary split/join preserve one packaged owner
versus two separate owners, complete nested type trees and ordered axes.
Composing them with unit/finish gives explicit left/right Unit maps with
coefficient +1. Scalar work on a removed Unit factor remains in the operator.
No implicit coherence, new native constructor or acceptance authority is added.

The existing finite split/join controls remain unchanged. Finite unit/finish,
selected coherent lifts, Raw tuple capabilities, general Basis support and
complete frontend convergence remain unfinished. This packet alone does not
close #43 or #32.

## Preserved sources and independent expectations

The first study is `authoring_sessions/quantum-tuple-unitors-v030/`: 22 complete
projects, 48 frozen input files, the original 44 observations with a failed
executable-identity check, and 44 stable repeated baseline observations.
Concurrent Cargo testing replaced the first observer's CLI. Those original
results were not rewritten; the stable repeat checks the executable before and
after each command. Its complete packet is separately bound by its files.json.

`independent-expectations.json` and 17 independent source files fix the exact
laws before testing. `independent-first-test.rs.txt` preserves the eleven-test
first draft; the corresponding JSON records its identity. Complete originals
of three existing tests and their minimal profile-assertion repairs remain in
`independent-prior-tests/`. Historical first sources are not migrated in place.
`initial-production/` retains the nine-file first implementation before
formatting, compiler execution and independent review.

Fixed external native requests independently specify the +1 unitors and their
round trips over seven small bases, retained omega scalar, tuple provider
inverse, eighth power and controlled fourth power. Full complex execution uses
nonfactorized reference-dimension-two coefficients; ordered-axis examples use
nonidentical amplitudes. Other source-event/instrument cases explicitly use a
producer consistency request plus independent action/event expectations; they
are not represented as independent external root equations. At most two
physical system qubits are used. Neither numerical comparison nor a native
accepted candidate proves general source preservation.

## Actual failures, review and repairs

`latest-first/` retains the initial integration success and new private test
failure. The first phased split/join mutant copied its circuit but left an
instrument wrapper referring to old fresh owners, so native acceptance rejected
it before the intended source-event check. `product-mutant-repair/` preserves
the formatted original and repair. The complete phased candidate payload,
graph and own request now remain consistent while original source metadata is
retained. Fresh native acceptance and actual omega coefficients precede the
required canonical-structural-tag rejection for both split and join.

`latest-resume/` then passed the library/native CLI checks and exposed a Clippy
item-placement failure. Independent review also found that event snapshots
counted ports but omitted internal nodes of an idle quantum basis tree. The
`trace-capacity-repair/` record preserves both repairs. The recorder charges
actual retained before/after and operand/result basis nodes before cloning,
while preserving previous Unit/Bit/Bits atom costs. A seven-node zero-width
basis and one H operation test rejection with an explicitly nearly-used budget
and acceptance with sufficient budget; no large input was generated. The
independent reviewer rechecked allocation order and unchanged state on rejection.

`policy-docs/` retains an initially stale public-surface coverage identity after
the inventory update. The reviewed readonly basis accessors, internal signature
and extended untrusted source domain are recorded in inventory-delta.json and
coverage-delta.json. Native routes, accepted-handle construction, external
schemas, pending proof gates and historical corpus pins are unchanged.

## Constitutional scope

QS-2026-01 requires exact ownership, full interface, phase and reference
correspondence. This work extends untrusted source preparation while keeping
fresh native structural/leaf acceptance and explicit source-event checks.
PR-2026-01's actual target-artifact correspondence and RS-2026-01's quantitative
program/resource bounds remain pending. Compiler storage limits are not the
quantitative Resource Safety theorem. EXACT-2026-01 is preserved without an
epsilon replacement. The two admitted ordinary QLV1 ownership/classical-scope
guarantees retain their original scope and evidence; they are not expanded to
source or hierarchy semantics by these tests. No interpretation, guarantee,
proof status, release version or constitutional text is changed.
